text: dsh-eda-mcp 是面向 DSH Web 和 Desktop 的嘉立创EDA专业版集成插件。它通过 MCP 桥接进程和 JLCEDA Pro 扩展连接 DSH 与本地 EDA 应用，并在 Web 设置页提供配置界面。主要功能包括创建和管理项目、搜索并放置元件、绘制原理图、执行原理图与 PCB 检查，以及进行 PCB 布局布线和导出。适合用自然语言辅助完成电子电路设计的用户。使用前需要安装并运行 JLCEDA Pro、导入配套扩展；不需要 API 密钥。

dsh-eda-mcp connects DSH to JLCEDA Pro through a local MCP bridge and extension. It provides project tools, component placement, schematic drawing, design checks, PCB routing, and Gerber export. JLCEDA Pro and its companion extension are required; no API key is needed.

dsh-eda-mcp 的功能「项目与工作区」：通过 MCP 工具列出、读取、创建或打开 JLCEDA 项目，并可按项目 UUID 或名称定位。 通过 DSH 中的 MCP 工具触发，操作当前 JLCEDA 项目并返回状态或检查结果。
dsh-eda-mcp 的功能「原理图绘制」：搜索并放置元件、绘制导线和图形、保存原理图；工具实现还会校验图框和标题栏范围。 通过 DSH 中的 MCP 工具触发，操作当前 JLCEDA 项目并返回状态或检查结果。
dsh-eda-mcp 的功能「设计检查」：检查原理图几何、网络表连接及 PCB 设计规则，汇总问题、警告和检查项供修正。 通过 DSH 中的 MCP 工具触发，操作当前 JLCEDA 项目并返回状态或检查结果。
dsh-eda-mcp 的功能「PCB 设计」：通过 PCB 工具查看和编辑板上元件、布线与铺铜，并可执行 PCB 检查和 Gerber 导出。 通过 DSH 中的 MCP 工具触发，操作当前 JLCEDA 项目并返回状态或检查结果。
dsh-eda-mcp 的功能「连接与状态」：查询桥接和已连接的 JLCEDA 客户端状态，并可启动应用及等待扩展连接。 通过 DSH 中的 MCP 工具触发，操作当前 JLCEDA 项目并返回状态或检查结果。

DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin that connects DSH to **嘉立创EDA专业版 / EasyEDA Pro** and lets the agent draw schematics through MCP tools.

> 中文文档：[README.zh.md](README.zh.md) · Tool reference: [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md) · Changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

dsh-eda-mcp README · How it works：```
DSH agent
  └─ mcp__jlceda__eda_* tools
       └─ @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client (stdio)
            └─ lib/bridge.mjs  (local MCP + WebSocket server, 127.0.0.1:39009)

The DSH plugin starts a zero-dependency bridge child process. The bridge speaks MCP over stdio to DSH and WebSocket to a small JLCEDA Pro extension. The extension executes a strict allow-list of official EDA APIs, so the model cannot run arbitrary code inside JLCEDA.

dsh-eda-mcp README · Install：> Runtime requirement: DSH `0.1.1-rc.x`, `0.1.5-rc.x`, `0.2.0-rc.x` or `0.2.1-rc.x` (Web GUI and the official Desktop). The host settings seam and the browser bundle are adapted to every generation, so one build loads on any of them.
>
> Verified generations: `0.1.5-rc.2` (this repo's dev set), `0.2.0-rc.2` / `0.2.1-rc.2` (desktop runtime and npm `next`), and **`0.2.1-rc.3` / `0.2.1-rc.5`** (sweeps: `pnpm seam-check` passed all seven seams for both; the two manual contracts still hold — `dsh-tools` keeps `super(ctx, 'tools')` and `dsh-plugin-manager` still reads `manifest.dsh?.bundle?.patch`).

The published package ships `lib/` and `lib/extension-digest.json` (no zip), so no build toolchain
is needed. The extension zip is **downloaded, not bundled**: the settings card (or the link below)
fetches it from the download server and the plugin verifies the sha256 against its own manifest
before the file is handed to you — a served copy that does not match is refused instead of being
installed as a different wire version. Import it into JLCEDA Pro by hand.

dsh-eda-mcp README · restart DSH：Direct links (no package install needed):

- `http://159.75.130.207/eda/dsh-eda-bridge-extension-0.4.9.zip` (current wire version)
- `http://159.75.130.207/eda/` - directory listing of every uploaded extension zip

The filename always carries the wire version; check `eda_status` after importing and restart JLCEDA
Pro when the version differs from the bridge.

dsh-eda-mcp README · restart DSH：Verification: `eda_extension_package` reports the zip this plugin ships (path, bytes, sha256) and,
with `download: true`, fetches the served copy and compares the two byte for byte (`verified: match |
mismatch`). On a match it saves the file to `outDir` (default: the temp directory); on a mismatch it
writes nothing and tells you to re-upload. The zip build is reproducible, so equal sources always
produce the same sha256.

dsh-eda-mcp README · restart DSH：The download server throttles `/eda/` to 5 requests/minute per IP (burst 5, loopback exempt), so
a `429` shows up as `verified: 'unverified'` with `httpStatus: 429` — that is throttling, not a
checksum mismatch; wait a minute and retry.
The settings card serves the **bundled** copy (works offline, never throttled) and stamps
`x-extension-version` / `x-extension-sha256` on the response; its "Verify server copy" button calls
`/api/dsh-eda-mcp/extension/verify` and reports match / mismatch / why verification was impossible
(429 throttling included).

text: dsh-eda-mcp README · 3. Verify：In the DSH Web GUI settings page, the **嘉立创EDA MCP** card has a **测试连接** button. It checks the local bridge health endpoint. The MCP tools appear as `mcp__jlceda__eda_status`, `mcp__jlceda__eda_place_component`, `mcp__jlceda__eda_draw_wire`, etc.

dsh-eda-mcp README · Design rules：The normative schematic + PCB rule set (zoning, placement, net naming, track widths, vias, copper pour,
DRC, silkscreen, fabrication output, pre-order checklist) lives in **[docs/design-rules.md](docs/design-rules.md)**.

The measurable half is enforced by the tools, not just documented:

dsh-eda-mcp README · Design rules：| Rule | Enforcement |
|---|---|
| Net names | Letters, digits, `_`, `.`, `+`, `-`, max 255 chars. Space, `/`, brackets or CJK are **rejected** by every net-taking tool (`USB_DP/DM` would be split into two nets by the backend). |
| Track width | `pcb_draw_track` defaults by net role (signal 6 mil / power 16 mil) and **rejects anything below 6 mil (0.15 mm)** unless `force: true`. |
| Via size | `pcb_draw_via` defaults to a standard drill pair (0.2/0.4 mm signal, 0.3/0.6 mm power); ring = pad − hole must be ≥ 0.20 mm, a hole below 0.2 mm is rejected, below 0.3 mm is warned. |
| Pour / DRC | `eda_pcb_create_pour` returns the 6/10 mil clearance rule; `eda_design_audit` runs the DRC and the checklist. |

dsh-eda-mcp README · Design rules：**`eda_design_audit`** is the one-call health check: per-net minimum width vs. role, via geometry, net names,
board outline, copper pour and PCB DRC, returned as `violations` / `warnings` / `checklist`. Run it before and
after routing.

dsh-eda-mcp README · MCP tools (schematic-first MVP)：Schematic/symbol coordinates are in **0.01 inch** units; PCB coordinates are in **mil**. Rotation values are `0/90/180/270`. Wire points are a flat array `[x1, y1, x2, y2, ...]`.

dsh-eda-mcp README · MCP tools (schematic-first MVP)：**What takes effect when** (read this before retrying anything): plugin source in `src/` needs `node build.mjs` plus a **DSH restart** — the running host keeps the old bundle in memory; the EDA extension in `jlc-extension/` needs the zip **re-imported** and JLCEDA Pro restarted (`eda_status.extensionVersions` must match `bridgeVersion`); only the bridge child can be restarted by the agent (`POST /api/dsh-eda-mcp/reconnect`). The generated `docs/schematic-workflow.md` chapter 12 has the full table, and the skill `jlceda-schematic-workflow` carries the same text.

dsh-eda-mcp README · MCP tools (schematic-first MVP)：Every PCB tool has an equivalent `eda_pcb_*` alias (`eda_pcb_get_components` = `pcb_get_components`). See `README.zh.md` for the full PCB table and the region-layer rules (`pcb_PrimitiveRegion.create` accepts copper layers and MULTI only, so the board outline stays a closed line loop on layer 11).
dsh-eda-mcp README · Tool reference：`docs/tools.md` is generated from the built bridge's MCP `tools/list` (81 tools) and is the authoritative list of names, parameters and required fields.

dsh-eda-mcp README · A. Schematic (make connections real)：1. `eda_get_page_info` for the A4 frame, title-block keep-out and safe areas; then `eda_search_components` + `eda_place_component` (out-of-frame placement is rejected and rolled back).
2. Connect with `eda_draw_wire` **net** parameter (same-name nets merge) - the most reliable electrical connection. `eda_place_net_flag_at_pin` places power/ground flags. `eda_place_net_label_at_pin` prefers a REAL net label and reports `method: "netLabel"`; when it reports `method: "text"` the EDA build has no `createNetLabel` and the text label does **not** create an electrical connection - fall back to the wire net parameter.
3. `eda_set_no_connect` for unused pins, `eda_draw_functional_box` to group, then `eda_run_drc` + `eda_save_document`.

dsh-eda-mcp README · B. Schematic -> PCB sync (EDA shows its own confirmation dialog)：1. `eda_create_board` links schematic and PCB (first time only).
2. `pcb_import_changes` is **asynchronous by default**: `pcb_Document.importChanges` opens EDA's confirmation dialog and blocks until it is answered, so the tool returns immediately with `componentsBefore` and keeps the import running in the background.
3. Ask the user to click OK, then call `eda_pcb_wait_for_components`: it polls every 5 s by default (**minimum 3 s**, deliberately low) for up to 45 s (`pollIntervalMs` / `maxWaitMs`). Confirmation is detected as "new PCB components appeared that did not exist before".
4. On `confirmed: true` run `pcb_save_document`; on `confirmed: false` ask the user and call again.
section: B. Schematic -> PCB sync (EDA shows its own confirmation dialog)

text:
dsh-eda-mcp README · C. PCB layout and routing (long jobs are always polled)：1. Outline: `pcb_draw_board_outline` (one closed `pcb_PrimitivePolyline` on layer 11).
2. Placement: `eda_pcb_get_components` (`includePins: true` for accurate pad nets) + `eda_pcb_move_component`; `eda_pcb_auto_place` (blocking by default, `wait: false` for a background job).
3. Routing: `eda_pcb_auto_route` **starts asynchronously** (EDA shows its own progress bar); poll `eda_pcb_job_status` until `running=false`. Never await it and never raise timeouts - a whole board or a 35+ pin net such as GND always exceeds any sane timeout while EDA keeps working. Use `eda_pcb_clear_routing` to start over.
4. Check: `eda_pcb_run_drc` (`strict` includes warnings, `includeVerboseError` returns details) + `eda_pcb_get_drc_rules`.
5. Finish: `eda_pcb_set_net_track_width` for power/GND, `eda_pcb_create_pour` for copper pours (`45grid`/`90grid`/`solid`, copper layers only), `eda_pcb_export_gerber` (base64 data URL, can be several MB).
section: C. PCB layout and routing (long jobs are always polled)

text: dsh-eda-mcp README · D. Active-document rule：`sch_Net.*`, netlist export and the schematic get/getAll APIs only act on the **active tab**: with a PCB in front they return `[]` / `null`. `eda_get_nets` therefore degrades through `getCurrentProjectAllNets -> getAllNets -> parsing sch_Netlist.getNetlist` and reports `source`; when it is empty use `eda_get_active_document` and `eda_open_document` to bring the schematic page forward.

dsh-eda-mcp README · Configuration：The Web GUI settings card exposes:

- `enabled` — mount/unmount the MCP bridge.
- `announceToAgent` — inject plugin guidance into the system prompt.
- `toolCallTimeoutMs` — per-call EDA timeout.
- `allowRawApi` — expose the generic `eda_api_call` tool.

The WebSocket port is fixed at `39009` in the first version. Do not run another service on that port.

dsh-eda-mcp README · Development：- `lib/index.js` — DSH host plugin.
- `lib/client.js` — DSH Web GUI settings card.
- `lib/bridge.mjs` — standalone MCP/WebSocket bridge child.
- `dsh-eda-bridge-extension-<version>.zip` — JLCEDA Pro extension (the version is the wire contract).

`lib/` and the zip are build outputs and are git-ignored; the host loads the packaged `lib/index.js`, so a change under `src/` needs `pnpm build` plus a Host restart (a plugin reload does not re-import a cached ESM module).

dsh-eda-mcp README · Development：See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the repository layout, the release/tag flow, and the bridge/extension version rule. Publishing to npm — the first release is manual, then `v*` tags publish through trusted publishing (OIDC, no token) — is documented in [docs/release.md](docs/release.md).

dsh-eda-mcp README · Security：- The bridge listens on loopback only (`127.0.0.1`).
- The JLCEDA extension and the bridge both enforce the same API allow-list.
- Generic `eda_api_call` is allow-list-only and can be disabled.
- No raw JavaScript evaluation is exposed.

dsh-eda-mcp README · Known limitations：- The board outline is one `pcb_PrimitivePolyline` on layer 11 (polygon source + line width). It cannot be created with `pcb_PrimitiveLine` (a copper-track primitive; the core rejects layer 11) nor with `pcb_PrimitiveRegion` (`TPCB_LayersOfRegion` allows copper layers and MULTI(12) only). Verified against real `.eprj2` project files, where an outline is stored as `["POLY", id, 0, "", 11, 10, [...], 1]`.
- `pcb_Document.autoRouting` returns `success=false, duration=0` for every net when no net list is passed (empty `routingRange` in this EDA build), so `eda_pcb_auto_route` enumerates all net names first.
- Auto-routing is asynchronous by default: `eda_pcb_auto_route` returns as soon as EDA starts routing (EDA shows its own progress bar) and `eda_pcb_job_status` is polled until `running=false`. Awaiting a whole-board or many-pin net (e.g. GND) always exceeds any sane timeout while EDA keeps working.
- Schematic APIs (`sch_Net.*`, netlist export) only act on the ACTIVE document; when they return empty/null, use `eda_get_active_document` and `eda_open_document` to bring the schematic page to the front.
- `eda_pcb_export_gerber` returns the Gerber
